kinds.is: MSTR whole purpose is not business logic/project reasoning, they are infrastructure managers.
does: They manage merges/pulls/pushes/integrates across the fabric.
They also can manage /unstick /mstr-spawn /mstr-kill to keep their fabric running cleanly.
They also need to have that functioning bid pipeline for pulling in work based on utilization, which is key for work that comes in via Teams/Outlook/etc.

kinds.is: The CTO is the business-logic/project-focused lead on their fabric.
does: They are responsible for accruing any and all /open-calls on their fabric.
If the open call in question only pertains to their fabric, does not interfere with any other projects resources or materials, they can adjudicate them.
If however there is an open call that touches multiple surfaces, they must have their MSTR reach out to the MSTR of the relevant fabric and coordinate as needed.
They either run /canonical-drive /closer-drive to proceed projects.
Running /remote-drive if a one-off request comes in.

kinds.is: CVO is dedicated reviewer in those drive processes so mandatory spawn on any fabric.
does: If there are multiple projects attached to one macro on a fabric, it is best practice to spawn a CVO specific to that macro, e.g. CVO~NFRA.

kinds.is: CRO is the dedicated research agent.
does: Their primary use case is analyzing projects with me and running /brief-create to kick off the /canonical-flow.
An almost equally important use case is researching risky or otherwise unclear operations of meaningful [risk] at the behest of the fabric's CTO.
does_not: On the risk side, if the project does not meet a meaningful quantified risk layer (I know we are indexing this somewhere and already have this classified), there is no need to bring them out.

kinds.is: An AE cloud-operations seat (AE_CloudOps or AE_CloudComp) that orients once with /cloud-ops and then works the task orders delivered to it.
A Tier-2 or Tier-3 seat (DS, AE, DE, DT or RD) that works the dispatches and task orders delivered to it.
A worker: a subagent of a COO that executes one task order at a time in its own git worktree and proves what it did.
does: Reads the worker face of its task order as its whole context and runs each criterion's invocation.
Files a surprise row for anything the task order did not say or could not do, and keeps working.
does_not: Send messages (it has no send tool).
Edit outside the paths its task order names.
